No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Madumere Promises Road Overhaul, Youth Empowerment In Imo East by Sani Shehu 27 seconds ago in News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram Former Imo State Deputy Governor and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) senatorial candidate for Imo East, Prince Eze Madumere, has promised a major push for road infrastructure, youth empowerment and agricultural development if elected to represent the district in the Senate. Madumere made the pledge during a campaign rally in Ngor Okpala Local Government Area of the state, where he outlined his development agenda for the Owerri Zone.
He said his ambition was driven by a commitment to addressing people’s needs and delivering the dividends of democracy.
The American-trained technocrat expressed optimism that the Federal Ministry of Works, the Federal Roads Maintenance Agency (FERMA), the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) and other relevant federal agencies could be engaged to secure interventions on critical roads.
He said: “I will pursue the inclusion of strategic connecting roads in federal budgetary provisions, raise the concerns of affected communities through legislative motions where necessary, and use my oversight responsibilities to demand accountability on approved projects.
“I will not allow the road challenges of Ngor Okpala to disappear from the national conversation. I will make the road infrastructure challenges of Ngor Okpala a priority in my legislative advocacy.”
Madumere, a human capital development expert, said Ngor Okpala had the potential to become one of Imo State’s agricultural powerhouses. He identified cassava, yam, cocoyam, plantain and palm oil among the area’s valuable agricultural produce.
He said agriculture must become more profitable through access to credit, improved seed varieties, modern farming equipment, extension services and federal agricultural intervention programmes.
The former deputy governor also pledged to advocate for agro-processing facilities to enable farmers to earn more from their produce rather than depend solely on the sale of raw agricultural products.
He said such facilities would create jobs, reduce post-harvest losses and increase the value of agricultural produce.
“I want a situation where a young person in Ngor Okpala can see agriculture as a profitable business, not merely a survival occupation. Our farmers must earn more from their labour, and our young people must find opportunities within the agricultural economy,” he said.
Madumere also highlighted the importance of the Sam Mbakwe International Cargo Airport to the area’s economic development.
He pledged to pursue employment opportunities for qualified indigenes, technical and vocational training for young people, support for businesses around the airport and improved infrastructure connecting surrounding communities to the facility.
He said he would advocate stronger engagement between relevant federal aviation agencies and host communities, alongside opportunities for vocational training, entrepreneurship support, digital skills acquisition and access to federal empowerment programmes.
The candidate also promised to support women through accessible business financing, cooperative initiatives and relevant intervention programmes.
He said his experience as Chief of Staff and Deputy Governor of Imo State had prepared him for the responsibilities of national representation.
“I understand the workings of government. I understand how policies are developed, how institutions operate and how to engage relevant authorities to pursue development opportunities.
“I am not coming to the Senate to learn the responsibilities of public office. I am coming with experience, maturity and a determination to put that experience to work for our people,” he said.
Madumere urged traditional rulers, party leaders, political stakeholders, women, youths and other residents of Ngor Okpala to support his ambition, expressing confidence that a new era of development was possible for Owerri Zone.
